beats.t: They ran down the corridor. When they reached Door Six, it was half open. Ivy stretched through the gap like ropes.
Neo hung at the end of the ivy, feet off the ground. Beneath his sleeves and shirt, dim light showed in place of a human body.
Neo! Why did you come alone?!
Those vines are wrapped around him!
Yeoni rushed in. The ivy lashed like a whip and knocked them to the floor. Blood welled on their scraped palms.
No hurry, vessel. He came of his own accord. To read his own name aloud.
His own name? That would open the door, but...
The reader pays the price. If Mr. Cat reads it, Mr. Cat disappears.
That's what he came to do? In our place?
Ivy wrapped Neo's mouth, preventing an answer. He looked at Yeoni with apologetic eyes. Those were the eyes Yeoni hated most.
But he could not finish. He cannot remember his own name. He offered it as payment.
So read it for him. Then the vines will release him.
A lie. That voice always tells only half the truth. I was deceived by that half too.
Is half not enough? It is true the vines will let go.
The ivy tightened. Neo faded further. Not even the outline of his right hand remained.
Matches! I've got matches!
Moka struck one. It died before the flame reached the ivy. The air before the door ate fire.
Even fire needs a name before this door. I'll draw the vines into the Void. I can't do it for long.
Yundal removed his glove. The black hole opened in his palm. Ivy dragged toward it. At the same time, his face went white.
Yeoni. Decide. I can last one minute.
Yeoni looked at the nameplate. As the ivy pulled away, the letters appeared. Park. Then the second syllable. Then the third.
(They told me not to read it. Hanbi and Neo both. But if I don't, Neo disappears.)
Yeoni. Don't read. There must be another way.
What if Neo disappears while we look? Hanbi, you waited at that bus stop too.
Seo Hanbi fell silent. It was true. No one knew better how a spring spent only waiting had ended.
Then I'll share responsibility. Whatever happens, half is mine.
Yeoni nodded and approached the nameplate. Neo shook his head urgently. Yeoni didn't stop.
Park. Byeong. Ha.
The moment the three syllables sounded, the nameplate burned white. The ivy scattered into ash. Neo fell.
Yeoni caught him. His face was still Neo's, the one who had been with them since the river. But over it appeared the man who had dropped a white umbrella at the bus stop.
It wasn't a new face. The face in a lost memory had finally connected to the one before them. The same person.
The person who came to the bus stop then... That was you?
Please don't ask that. Answering would break the rules.
Neo smiled. At that instant, the seal on his name broke, and light drained from his toes upward. Knees, waist, chest. Beneath Yeoni's hands, he grew fainter.
I knew this would happen if the seal broke. Let me catch my breath. Just a moment.
It's not just a moment! Your body's disappearing!
The escaping light barely stopped at his chest. Neo still looked human, but his lower body blurred like a reflection in water. Yeoni refused to release the unseen hand.
My voice still works. There should be time to explain.
Then explain. Everything this time. Leave nothing out. I have to know so we can find a way together.
Neo looked at Moka, Yundal, then Seo Hanbi. Finally, Yeoni. It was time to speak of what he had hidden behind his name.
In the first spring, I knew you. Same school, same bus stop. You were always losing umbrellas.
That night I knew something was wrong with your phone, but I couldn't knock on your door. I thought I'd tell you tomorrow.
I'm also the one who opened the door that night. Park Byeongha paid with his body and name and returned as Yeongnyangi. You called me Neo.
Then from the start... you remembered a future where I disappeared?
Yes. I went back in time exactly once. To prevent that ending in this spring.
I was caught in the door Byeongha opened and followed him through. I was only a companion who knew the first spring. The one who turned time back was Yeongnyangi—Neo—Park Byeongha.
The next day, I ran to the bus stop. Too late. You were no longer you.
So that's what you meant. 'Too late. Again.'
Neo bowed his head slightly to Seo Hanbi. Same spring, same bus stop. The one who arrived late and the one who waited to the end faced each other.
After that, I called customer support every day. The place called the universe. My place in the queue was always infinity.
I don't know which winter it was. Someone finally answered. They would give me one more chance.
The price?
You must not know my name. If my name is spoken, I return to my original place. A place of nothing.
Then I just spoke it. I sent you away.
Half of me. The door took half for the price of one name. The remaining half can hold on if you don't say it again.
Then why didn't you tell me sooner? I wouldn't have read it.
Because telling you would have been the same as giving you my name.
This cat, honestly. His logic actually works, which makes me even angrier.
Yundal approached while pulling his glove on. His hand shook. He had held the Void open too long.
So that's why your place was borrowed, Mr. Cat. Gyeong, in the Hour column of Yeoni's Four Pillars.
[ Year: Im-o · Month: Byeong-o · Day: Eulhae · Hour: Gyeong-Chen ] Gyeong · Flickering
You pledged your name to occupy someone else's Four Pillars. The Direct Officer position. I've never seen a contract like that.
What was Direct Officer again? Isn't that the husband's position?
Is this the time?!
Let's leave that conversation for later.
For an instant, there was laughter. But when the wall's pattern showed through Neo's shoulder, no one could follow it with another joke.
Beyond the door lay the garden of Card Six. An angel spread its wings between two trees. Beneath it, the path forked.
The Lovers isn't a card of love. It's a card of choice. We have to choose one of the two to pass.
A sign stood before each path. This time the words were clear. Black Moon had kindly written them out.
[ Left · Remember the name—he disappears ] [ Right · Forget the name—he remains ]
An easy choice, is it not? Forget. Even forgotten, he stays beside you. A nameless beast.
That isn't staying.
Stay out of this, rainwater. The choice belongs to the vessel.
Something was dragged from Yeoni's mind. The middle syllable of the name blurred. Yeoni pressed their forehead. The name they had just read was leaking between their fingers.
Wait. The middle. What was the middle syllable?
Forget it. That's right. Go right.
Are you siding with Black Moon?
I'm siding with you. I always have.
Yeoni stood between the signs. Looked left. Looked right. Then took out their notebook and pulled the pen cap off with their teeth.
I don't want either.
You cannot pass without choosing.
I'll choose. But not what you've written.
Yeoni wrote in large letters, pressing hard. Almost hard enough to tear the paper.
[ Even in a different form, Neo. On my side. ]
I won't say your name, because you'll disappear. But I won't forget you either. I'll use the name I gave you instead.
Neo. Hey, Neo. You're Neo. That's what I called you. Since the day we met.
The ground split between the two signs. A third path appeared, narrow and uneven. It had no sign.
Neo's fingertips grew a little clearer. Yeoni took his hand again. This time, they could feel the outline of his fingers.
This path wasn't in the contract.
That's why people don't trust fortune-tellers. They insist on making a third path.
Nonsense. A made-up name is no name.
That nonsense saved me too. The name Hanbi.
Black Moon didn't answer. The angel in the garden folded its wings. At the path's end stood Door Seven, painted with a wheeled chariot.
Yeoni knelt to meet Neo's eyes. Their hand passed through his cheek when they tried to touch it. Still, they didn't withdraw. They held their palm where he should have been.
The middle syllable really is gone. Park, then Ha. That's all that's left.
That's enough. Remembering all of it is dangerous.
Even if it's dangerous, I wanted to remember. It's your name.
Neo is enough for me. You've called me by the name you gave me longer than by my original one.
Neo closed his eyes. Their light slowly faded. His head tilted like someone who had held on too long.
I'll sleep a little. You can scold me again when I wake.
You'd better wake up. If you don't, one star.
As his body faded further, Yeoni couldn't support him alone. Yundal took his other arm. Moka held the back of his shirt.
Wheels sounded inside Door Seven. Together, they supported Neo and laid him on the chariot's seat. His thin breaths continued.
